exact_claims.statement: With gamma, degree limits, B0, xi, T, zeta and finally X chosen in that order, the finite bound gives one block choice making at least half the points regular, and at every scheduled step i the good cumulative prime product is at least X^(delta_(h_i)+gamma/2), uniformly over points and other blocks.

The dependence-sensitive mechanism from the actual evaluation kernels through rank records, deletion and cumulative good-prime products is valid with the explicit finite-pool error D/(n-ell-T+2). This verifies that mechanism only, not the determinant cut, counting tree, large-prime tail or density theorem.

source: Old Argus report.md:321-423; OpenAI September 24, 2026 manuscript, Section 3:169-184,298-406,473-485.
assessment: The ordered constants have no X-dependent circularity; elementary prime-pool growth, the uniform conditional finite bound, Markov and the union bound give common regular points. The all-path definition of bad primes licenses reuse of earlier blocks and gives every stated cumulative threshold. This supports the adaptive subsystem, not the separate residue-cut input or the whole affine theorem.
hypotheses: Fixed r,N, positive epsilon and delta_h, fixed weighted-box and total-component geometric complexity.
Common ordinary stage degrees fixed before prime choices; uniform integer record cap B0 and nonzero minor product height X^K.
Uniform finite deletion estimate conditional on arbitrary other-block choices.
Disjoint growing pools of distinct primes between X^zeta and 32 X^zeta, after all constants including D=floor(K/zeta) are fixed.
supported_scope: Explicit gamma, xi, T, zeta and ell_i schedule and positive finite-pool denominator.
Elementary sufficient prime-pool growth, without importing an unverified prime-distribution citation.
A single block choice with at least half the original points regular, without independence of full minors or bad events.
Good cumulative product at least X^(delta_(h_i)+gamma/2) for every regular point and scheduled stage.
The conjunction of the finite theorem and actual-kernel and height bridges as a conditional adaptive submechanism.

external_assumptions.statement: The separate residue-cut lemma supplies bounded degrees uniformly from a fixed positive margin and bounded patch degrees, independently of primes and initial coefficient heights.
external_assumptions.status: Explicit external-to-this-unit input; only its statement and compatibility with the choice order were checked, not its determinant proof.
